strategies.label: Global stock market
strategies.explainer: Every listed company in the world, weighted by size. The simplest possible 'do nothing' portfolio and the fairest yardstick for a stock-heavy strategy.

strategies.label: Global 80/20
strategies.explainer: Global stocks with a fifth in bonds. A common setting for someone decades from retirement who still wants some cushion.

strategies.label: Global 60/40
strategies.explainer: The classic balanced portfolio. Lower highs and shallower lows.

strategies.label: Target-date 2060 fund
strategies.explainer: One fund that holds global stocks and bonds and gets more conservative as you age. What most 401k plans use as a default.

strategies.label: US stock market
strategies.explainer: Every US-listed company, weighted by size.
strategies.caution: US stocks beat global stocks over the last decade. Nobody knew that in advance, and the reverse has happened in other decades. Treat this as context, not as a standard your strategy should have met.

strategies.label: S&P 500
strategies.caution: This is the single most hindsight-prone comparison available. US large caps had an exceptional run; picking them in advance would have been a concentrated bet, not prudence. Shown for context only.

strategies.label: All bonds
strategies.explainer: The whole US investment-grade bond market. Useful as a floor reference.
